segments.narration: Somewhere in Russia a radio has buzzed since 1982. Nobody has ever claimed it.
Tune a shortwave receiver to 4625 kilohertz and it is there: a flat tone, about twenty-five buzzes a minute, day and night.
Then on Christmas Eve 1997 the buzzing stopped. A Russian voice read out a string of numbers and one word: golosok. Then the buzzing came back.
So is it a doomsday trigger? Listeners nicknamed it exactly that, but it has been knocked off air more than once and nothing followed.

The best answer is duller and stranger. It looks like a channel marker for a Russian military network, holding one frequency occupied so nobody else takes it. The buzz is not the message. The buzz is the fence.
